title: My solo project where the main rule is: grab literally anything, build a terrible bridge, and try not to die.
author: CrystalHare0
selftext:
Hi everyone, Crystal here!

I’m working on a solo hobby project – a co-op game to play with friends. The core mechanic is all about improvisation: you basically grab whatever you can find, build a makeshift bridge out of it, and try your best not to die. I’m also planning to add some smaller puzzles along the way.I’d love to hear your thoughts on this! What do you think I could change, improve, or add to the project?Thanks and cheers! :)

comments.author: DisasterNarrow4949
comments.body: For a game about bridge building, this showcase have a severe lack of bridge building.

replies.author: CrystalHare0
replies.body: You're right. I focused on the funny situations :D

comments.author: IllConsideration9821
comments.body: This is really cool! I can tell you put a lot of time into it. 😊

replies.author: CrystalHare0
replies.body: Oh, you meant split-screen, not a screenshot xD —I misunderstood sorry 😆. That would be pretty hard for me to pull off; I’ve never even tried doing it, though it would certainly be a great solution.

comments.author: Water-Cheese
comments.body: Looks great! What was your workflow for the environments and models?

replies.author: CrystalHare0
replies.body: Thanks! :) Since I don't know how to create models myself, I sourced them from the internet; however, regarding level design, I try to create it as if I were the player myself.

replies.author: Water-Cheese
replies.body: Nice! You've done a great job and piecing everything together, I like it! What engine are you using?

replies.author: CrystalHare0
replies.body: Thank you :) Personally I use Unity

comments.author: Ok_Leadership_429
comments.body:
Hi Crystal! Okay this looks genuinely great, the town itself has so much personality, the water tower, the little house with the fire pit and chairs out front, that bridge in the background, it all feels like a real place people would actually want to hang out and mess around in with friends. The lighting is doing a lot of work too, that warm afternoon glow makes everything feel cozy rather than sterile, which is exactly the vibe a "grab whatever and improvise" co-op game should have.

"Build a terrible bridge and try not to die" might be one of the most honest and charming pitches I've seen on this sub in a while, it tells you everything about the tone of the game in one line, chaotic but fun, not trying to be some big serious survival game. That kind of clarity in a pitch is genuinely rare and it already makes me want to play it with friends just from reading it.

Really solid presentation overall for a solo hobby project, this doesn't feel like an early prototype, it feels like something with a clear identity already. What's the wildest object someone's managed to turn into a "bridge piece" so far in testing?

replies.author: CrystalHare0
replies.body: Omg, thanks. It’s really great to hear that someone would want to play something I created. As for the bridges—honestly, I don't have a photo of any funny-looking bridge right now, other than the one at the end of the trailer. Thanks for the kind words, it means a lot to me and keeps me motivated to keep working. Best regards! :)

comments.author: PerfectSituation1668
comments.body: That looks like fun! You can add challenges, puzzles, maybe a funny story as why they do that. Any game with friends added is added fun to the game, because of the friends. But maybe also give it some solo/testing room/area for people to test it and lock the rest of the game behind co-op. It has that Gary's mod vibe. I like the freedom it gives you with friends. Looking forward on your progress.

replies.author: CrystalHare0
replies.body: Thank you so much for your feedback :)
